views.name: player_latest_attributes
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  pa.id AS id,
  pa.player_fifa_api_id AS player_fifa_api_id,
  pa.player_api_id AS player_api_id,
  pa.date AS date,
  pa.overall_rating AS overall_rating,
  pa.potential AS potential,
  pa.preferred_foot AS preferred_foot,
  pa.attacking_work_rate AS attacking_work_rate,
  pa.defensive_work_rate AS defensive_work_rate,
  pa.crossing AS crossing,
  pa.finishing AS finishing,
  pa.heading_accuracy AS heading_accuracy,
  pa.short_passing AS short_passing,
  pa.volleys AS volleys,
  pa.dribbling AS dribbling,
  pa.curve AS curve,
  pa.free_kick_accuracy AS free_kick_accuracy,
  pa.long_passing AS long_passing,
  pa.ball_control AS ball_control,
  pa.acceleration AS acceleration,
  pa.sprint_speed AS sprint_speed,
  pa.agility AS agility,
  pa.reactions AS reactions,
  pa.balance AS balance,
  pa.shot_power AS shot_power,
  pa.jumping AS jumping,
  pa.stamina AS stamina,
  pa.strength AS strength,
  pa.long_shots AS long_shots,
  pa.aggression AS aggression,
  pa.interceptions AS interceptions,
  pa.positioning AS positioning,
  pa.vision AS vision,
  pa.penalties AS penalties,
  pa.marking AS marking,
  pa.standing_tackle AS standing_tackle,
  pa.sliding_tackle AS sliding_tackle,
  pa.gk_diving AS gk_diving,
  pa.gk_handling AS gk_handling,
  pa.gk_kicking AS gk_kicking,
  pa.gk_positioning AS gk_positioning,
  pa.gk_reflexes AS gk_reflexes,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY pa.player_api_id ORDER BY datetime(pa.date) DESC) AS latest_attr_rank
FROM player_attributes pa

params.when_to_use: Find the latest attributes/ratings row for each player_api_id (one row per player_api_id) according to the view's internal ranking — e.g. show each player's most recent scouting/attributes snapshot. | Join player-level time-varying attributes to a dataset that already has one row per player_api_id (or is intended to be at the player_api_id grain) and you want the single latest attribute record. | Answer questions about the attribute values as-of the view's chosen latest observation (e.g. latest overall_rating, preferred_foot, gk_reflexes) for each player_api_id.
params.when_not_to_use: Do not use this view when you need all attribute history rows per player_api_id — this view returns only the 'latest' row (ranking applied). Using it will silently drop older observations. | Do not use this view to get the latest attributes as-of a specific date or match context different from the view's ranking rule — the view applies its own ROW_NUMBER() partitioning and may choose a different 'latest' row than a date-bound filter would. This will produce wrong time-conditioning. | Do not use this view when you need a different grain than player_api_id (for example player_api_id × date, per-match/player lineup, per-team aggregates) — joining it into a dataset at a finer grain will duplicate the latest row across multiple child rows and lead to inflated counts/incorrect aggregations. | Do not use this view to compute aggregates across time (e.g. average rating over time) — it contains exactly one snapshot per player_api_id, so temporal aggregates will be incorrect if you expect history. | Do not rely on this view for cohort selection where the cohort depends on attribute values at different moments (e.g. players whose rating exceeded X at any time) — the view only exposes the chosen latest record and will miss players who met a condition earlier but not at the latest snapshot. | Do not use this view for GK-specific analyses that need all goalkeeper observations if latest_attr_rank is not the intended selector — the view exposes gk_* fields only for the chosen latest row and may hide variability across time.
params.comparison: use team_latest_attributes(RANK) instead when you need the latest attribute snapshot but at the team grain — that sibling performs an analogous latest-ranking logic for teams rather than players. | use match_player_lineups_unified(RESHAPE) instead when you need player attributes contextualized per match lineup (per match × player) — that sibling is reshaped to the match-player grain and will not silently drop or duplicate match-level rows. | use match_basic_summary(AGG) instead when you want aggregated match-level metrics (team or match aggregates) rather than one-row-per-player snapshots — aggregating player_latest_attributes into match summaries will double-count if joined at the wrong key. | use player_master_demographics(NORM) instead when you need stable, non-time-varying player identifiers/demographics (name, birth date, nationality) — player_latest_attributes contains time-varying attribute snapshots and may differ from normalized master records.

views.description: Latest Player_Attributes snapshot per player_api_id (one row per player_api_id) with attribute measures. Use when you need each player's most recent observable attributes for joins, comparisons, or ranking. | Use for: Compare current overall_rating or potential across players; Join most-recent player attributes to player master for demographics; Find players above/below thresholds using latest attributes; Top-K players by overall_rating using latest snapshot (filter where latest_attr_rank=1 then rank)

views.name: team_latest_attributes
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  team_fifa_api_id,
  team_api_id,
  date,
  buildUpPlaySpeed,
  buildUpPlaySpeedClass,
  buildUpPlayDribbling,
  buildUpPlayDribblingClass,
  buildUpPlayPassing,
  buildUpPlayPassingClass,
  buildUpPlayPositioningClass,
  chanceCreationPassing,
  chanceCreationPassingClass,
  chanceCreationCrossing,
  chanceCreationCrossingClass,
  chanceCreationShooting,
  chanceCreationShootingClass,
  chanceCreationPositioningClass,
  defencePressure,
  defencePressureClass,
  defenceAggression,
  defenceAggressionClass,
  defenceTeamWidth,
  defenceTeamWidthClass,
  defenceDefenderLineClass,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY team_api_id ORDER BY datetime(date) DESC) AS latest_team_attr_rank
FROM Team_Attributes

params.when_to_use: Get the latest Team_Attributes row per team_api_id (i.e., the most recent dated attributes for each team). Use when you need the most-recent snapshot of team attribute fields for each team. | Join a team-level dataset (one row per team_api_id) to enrich it with the current/latest team attribute values. | Power displays or exports that show the current attribute values (buildUpPlaySpeed, defenceAggression, etc.) for each team without aggregation beyond selecting the single latest row.
params.when_not_to_use: Do not use to compute aggregated statistics across multiple attribute records (e.g., average buildUpPlaySpeed over time): the view returns only a row rank per team; it does not aggregate across time and selecting rows with latest_team_attr_rank > 1 will return older versions rather than an aggregate. | Do not use when you need attributes at a different grain than team_api_id (for example, match-level team attributes or player-level attributes). This view is partitioned by team_api_id and returns one or more rows per team depending on how you filter by latest_team_attr_rank. | Do not assume this view already filters to only the latest row per team unless you explicitly filter WHERE latest_team_attr_rank = 1. Without that filter it will return every Team_Attributes row with an added rank column, which can silently duplicate teams and inflate counts. | Do not use to get attributes as-of a specific match date or snapshot prior to the most recent date: the ORDER BY datetime(date) DESC chooses the most recent available date, not a date-at-or-before a supplied match date. | Do not use for cohort filtering (e.g., teams active in a season) unless you also apply the appropriate season/match filters; this view has no season or match identifiers and can include rows outside the cohort of interest. | Do not rely on id being unique across teams: id is passed through from Team_Attributes and may be the row id for that specific record; because the view can include multiple rows per team (unless filtered), counting ids without filtering by latest_team_attr_rank can miscount teams.
params.comparison: use player_latest_attributes(RANK) instead when you need the same 'latest per entity' logic at the player grain — player_latest_attributes partitions by player identifier and returns the latest player attribute rows, whereas team_latest_attributes partitions by team_api_id and is for teams. | use match_player_lineups_unified(RESHAPE) instead when you need match-level or lineup-level player occurrences — that view is reshaped to match-player-lineup grain, whereas team_latest_attributes is not tied to matches. | use match_basic_summary(AGG) instead when you need aggregated match-level team statistics (goals, shots, etc.): match_basic_summary performs match-level aggregations and includes match context, whereas team_latest_attributes is a point-in-time attribute snapshot without match aggregation. | use player_master_demographics(NORM) instead when you need normalized demographic data for players: player_master_demographics provides a normalized player-centric master table, while team_latest_attributes provides team attribute snapshots and is unrelated to player demographics. | use league_with_country(JOIN) when you need league-to-country joins or context for competitions: league_with_country joins league and country information, while team_latest_attributes only exposes team attribute fields and does not include league or competition context.

views.description: Latest Team_Attributes snapshot per team_api_id (one row per team_api_id) exposing tactical/attribute measures and classes. Use to join a team's most recent tactical profile to matches or aggregate by league/country. | Use for: Join most-recent team tactical attributes to Match by home_team_api_id/away_team_api_id; Aggregate team attribute distributions across leagues or seasons; Filter teams by a tactical class (e.g., buildUpPlaySpeedClass) using latest snapshot

params.when_to_use: List every player who was listed in any home or away slot for each match (one row per match id + slot_name). Use when you need a long/unnested roster of match slots with the associated match metadata (match_api_id, season, date, home_team_api_id, away_team_api_id). | Count or filter by slot-level attributes (e.g., how many times a particular player appeared in any specific slot name like 'home_player_3'). | Create per-match, per-slot joins to player tables (e.g., to pull player attributes into the exact slot positions). | Build lineups that preserve the original slot identity (slot_name) and side ('home' or 'away') for each match.
params.when_not_to_use: Do not use when you need one row per match with aggregated lineups (e.g., lists/arrays of players or counts per team). This view is long-form (one row per slot) and will over-count if you aggregate by match without deduplicating or pivoting. | Do not use when you need only starters/substitutes/cohort filtered by actual participation. The view reflects stored slot fields (home_player_1..home_player_11 and away_player_1..away_player_11) regardless of whether the player actually played; treating these as 'played' can silently miscount appearances. | Do not use when you need the current (latest) attributes of players or teams — the view only exposes player_api_id and match-level metadata; it does not join to player_latest_attributes or team_latest_attributes, so attributes may be missing or stale. | Do not use when you need a deduplicated list of unique players per match or per team without handling NULLs: slot columns that are NULL become rows with NULL player_api_id, which can lead to incorrect counts or joins if not filtered. | Do not use when you need away-side rows — the provided SQL fragment only shows 'home' rows (and the SQL is truncated). Reuse without verifying the full definition may miss the away side entirely, producing incorrect cohorts.
params.comparison: use player_latest_attributes instead when you need up-to-date player-level attributes — that view is ranked to give the latest attribute rows per player, whereas match_player_lineups_unified only provides player_api_id in the context of a match slot. | use match_basic_summary instead when you need one row per match with aggregated summary fields — match_basic_summary is an aggregate by match (AGG), while match_player_lineups_unified is long/reshaped (one row per slot) and will produce multiple rows per match. | use player_master_demographics instead when you need stable demographic keys for players across datasets — that normalized table supplies canonical player metadata, whereas this view only supplies the player_api_id and match context. | use team_latest_attributes when you need current team attributes for joins on home_team_api_id or away_team_api_id — this view provides the team ids but not their attributes or rankings.

views.description: Unpivot match lineup player references into one row per match/player/side/slot preserving both numbering schemes where available. Use to analyze player participation, compute per-player match counts, or join to Player/Player_Attributes. | Use for: Count matches played per player in a season; Join player latest attributes to matches via match_player_lineups_unified.player_api_id; Filter lineups for players on a given side/team

views.name: match_basic_summary
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  match_api_id,
  country_id,
  league_id,
  season,
  stage,
  date,
  home_team_api_id,
  away_team_api_id,
  home_team_goal,
  away_team_goal,
  (home_team_goal - away_team_goal) AS goal_diff,
  possession,
  B365H,
  B365D,
  B365A,
  BWH,
  BWD,
  BWA,
  IWH,
  IWD,
  IWA,
  LBH,
  LBD,
  LBA,
  PSH,
  PSD,
  PSA,
  WHH,
  WHD,
  WHA,
  SJH,
  SJD,
  SJA,
  VCH,
  VCD,
  VCA,
  GBH,
  GBD,
  GBA,
  BSH,
  BSD,
  BSA
FROM Match

params.when_to_use: Retrieve one row per Match.id with match-level columns (ids, teams, score, basic stats and available bookmaker odds) for analyses that require the canonical match record as stored in the Match table. | Join by Match.id (or match_api_id when present and unique) to get match metadata (season, stage, date, home/away team ids, goals, possession) for downstream joins that expect one row per match. | Compute simple per-match derived values (e.g., goal_diff as home_team_goal - away_team_goal) or filter/select matches by league_id, country_id, season, stage, or date before further aggregation.
params.when_not_to_use: Do not reuse when you need player- or team-season-level aggregates (e.g., "goals per player" or "team season summary") — this view is at match-grain (one row per match.id) and will double-count if aggregated across players or lineups. | Do not reuse for lineups/cohort-of-players queries (for example, "players who started in match X") — it contains only match-level team ids, not per-player lineup rows; using it in place of a lineup table will silently produce incorrect counts (one row per match instead of multiple players). | Do not reuse when you need time-series at a finer temporal grain than the match (for example, minute-by-minute events) — this view has only a match-level date and no event timestamps, so temporal analyses requiring event-level granularity will be incorrect or incomplete. | Do not reuse when you need normalized player demographic fields or player-level attributes — those are in player_master_demographics and player_latest_attributes; substituting this view will miss or misattribute player-level columns. | Do not reuse when you need bookmaker odds merged from multiple sources per match outcome if you expect multiple bookmaker rows per match — this view selects a single set of columns from Match; if your source data had multiple odds rows per match, this view does not represent that multiplicity and will hide duplicates. | Do not reuse as an aggregated summary across seasons/leagues without re-aggregating explicitly — aggregating this view without considering match as the grain (e.g., counting rows as teams or players) will produce misleading totals.
params.comparison: use player_latest_attributes instead when you need the latest per-player attribute snapshot — it has player-grain RANK and contains per-player attribute columns that are absent from this match-grain view. | use team_latest_attributes instead when you need the latest per-team attribute snapshot — it has team-grain RANK and team-specific attributes, whereas match_basic_summary is match-grain and only contains team ids. | use match_player_lineups_unified instead when you need one row per player appearance (lineup/substitute) in a match — match_player_lineups_unified is reshaped to the player-appearance grain; match_basic_summary is one row per match and will undercount or lose player-level detail. | use player_master_demographics instead when you need normalized player demographic fields (e.g., birthdate, nationality) — that view is normalized for player demographic data and match_basic_summary does not contain those columns. | use league_with_country when you need league metadata joined to country information — league_with_country performs a join to include country-level metadata, while match_basic_summary only exposes league_id and country_id foreign keys and not the joined country fields.

views.description: One row per Match summarizing basic measures and results: goals, possession (as text), and common bookmaker odds. Use for match-level analytics, joining to league/team or aggregating across seasons. | Use for: Aggregate average odds by league/season; Analyze goal differentials by team/season; Filter matches with missing odds or compute derived win probabilities

views.name: player_master_demographics
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  player_api_id,
  player_name,
  player_fifa_api_id,
  birthday,
  CASE WHEN birthday IS NOT NULL AND trim(birthday) != '' THEN CAST((julianday(date('now')) - julianday(birthday))/365.25 AS INTEGER) ELSE NULL END AS age_years,
  height,
  weight
FROM Player

params.when_to_use: Get one row per Player (id) with basic identity and physical attributes: player_api_id, player_name, player_fifa_api_id, birthday, computed age_years, height, weight. | Join player-level static demographic attributes to other tables by Player.id (e.g., enrich a roster table or attribute history table that is keyed by player id). | Filter or report on players' demographic cohorts (e.g., all players born before 1990, or players older than 30) where one row per player is required.
params.when_not_to_use: Do not use this view when you need the latest attributes per player at a point in time — this view returns the raw Player table row(s) and not the most-recent attributes by date. Using it for time-specific attribute snapshots will silently give incorrect cohorts/values. | Do not use when you need a roster or lineup-level grain (one row per match-player or per lineup). This view is at player-grain (id); joining it directly to match-player rows can produce duplication or incorrect counts if match-level rows multiply players. | Do not use when you need aggregated player counts (e.g., number of players per team or per age bracket) without first ensuring de-duplication: if the underlying Player table contains multiple rows per logical player id in your DB, counts may be inflated. This view assumes one row per id. | Do not use when you need attributes that are stored in separate attributes/history tables (e.g., dynamic height/weight changes). This view only exposes columns present on the Player table and will miss any later updates captured in attribute history. | Do not use when you require timezone- or snapshot-accurate age calculations. age_years is computed relative to the current date (date('now')) and will change over time; using it for historical analysis will silently misrepresent ages at past match dates.
params.comparison: use player_latest_attributes instead when you need the most-recent attribute values per player (time-aware) — player_latest_attributes is a RANK view that resolves latest rows by date, whereas player_master_demographics exposes raw Player columns and a current-date age calculation. | use match_player_lineups_unified instead when you need match-level or lineup-level rows (one row per match-player) — match_player_lineups_unified is reshaped to the match-player grain, whereas player_master_demographics is one row per player and will multiply or undercount if naively joined to match data. | use match_basic_summary when you need aggregated match-level statistics (counts, aggregates) — match_basic_summary produces aggregated match-level outputs, whereas player_master_demographics is not aggregated and will not correctly answer match- or team-level aggregation questions. | use team_latest_attributes when joining to team-level latest info — team_latest_attributes provides team-grain latest attributes (RANK), while player_master_demographics is player-grain and should not substitute for team-level joins or metrics. | use league_with_country when you need league-to-country joins — league_with_country is a JOIN view that enriches league info with country details; player_master_demographics has no league or country context and cannot replace that join.

views.description: Cleaned player master table projecting identifier and demographic fields useful for joins: player_api_id, player_name, player_fifa_api_id, birthday, age_years (derived), height, weight. Age is computed relative to current_date() via julianday for reuse; may be NULL when birthday is NULL. | Use for: Filter players by age range or height/weight; Join player demographics to attributes or match participation; Compute age distributions per league/season after joining matches

views.name: league_with_country
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  League.id AS id,
  League.country_id AS country_id,
  League.name AS name,
  Country.id AS country_id__country,
  Country.name AS name__country
FROM League
LEFT JOIN Country ON League.country_id = Country.id

params.when_to_use: When you need a one-row-per-league canonical record with league-level attributes (league id, league name, and the associated country id and country name). | When you need to join league-level information into other datasets at the league grain (i.e., to enrich rows that are already at League.id grain). | When you need to show or export league metadata (e.g., lists of leagues with their country names) without applying additional aggregations or temporal logic.
params.when_not_to_use: Do not use this view when you need aggregated metrics across leagues (e.g., counts of teams or players per league) — this view is not aggregated and will cause double counting if joined to many-to-one child tables without first grouping/aggregating the child side. | Do not use this view when you need a different grain (e.g., team-level, player-level, match-level). The view's grain is League.id; joining it to finer-grained facts without proper keys or filtering will produce incorrect multiplicative results. | Do not use this view when you need a time-aware or versioned snapshot of league attributes. This view returns the current/declared League rows only (no rank/version/time dimension), so it will be silently wrong for historical or latest-per-period analyses. | Do not use this view when you need to filter or identify rows by country attributes for cohort definitions unless you account for NULL countries: the join is LEFT JOIN, so leagues without a country_id will still appear with NULL country fields — using this view as a cohort source can include unintended NULL-country leagues. | Do not use this view when you expect canonical country rows (one row per country). The view repeats country fields at the league grain (country appears once per league). For country-level analyses you must use a country-level view or reduce this view by country_id first.
params.comparison: use player_latest_attributes instead when you need the latest time-ranked attributes for players — player_latest_attributes has RANK semantics and returns the most recent attribute row per player, whereas league_with_country has no temporal ranking and is static at League.id grain. | use team_latest_attributes instead when you need team-level canonical attributes — team_latest_attributes provides team-grain (and likely rank/temporal) information, while league_with_country is league-grain and will not correctly substitute for team data. | use match_player_lineups_unified instead when working with per-match player lineup rows — that view is a reshaped, match-level/fine-grained dataset appropriate for match-by-match analyses; league_with_country is coarse and will cause incorrect multiplicity if joined directly to match-player rows. | use match_basic_summary instead when you need aggregated match-level metrics — match_basic_summary is an AGG view designed to produce one row per match with aggregated stats; joining league_with_country to raw match rows without matching aggregation levels can miscount events. | use player_master_demographics when you need normalized, person-level demographic details — player_master_demographics is NORM (person-grain normalized data) and includes demographic cohort logic, whereas league_with_country contains only league and related country attributes and lacks person-level cohort semantics.

views.description: Denormalized League rows joined to Country to expose league name and country name. Use when reporting or aggregating by country or when joining matches to country-level labels. | Use for: Show leagues and their countries for match-level aggregations; Group matches by Country.name via league join
